by all accounts	prepositional phrase	据大家所说	By all accounts, the missing cat has been eating breakfast at several different houses.	据大家所说，那只失踪的猫一直在好几户人家吃早饭。
by all appearances	prepositional phrase	从外表判断	By all appearances, the dusty suitcase had not been opened for years.	从外表看，那个落满灰尘的手提箱已经多年没有打开过了。
by any chance	prepositional phrase	万一	If by any chance the parcel arrives early, please put it in the shed.	万一包裹提前到了，请把它放进棚子里。
by appointment	prepositional phrase	按预约	We visited the little costume collection by appointment on a rainy afternoon.	一个下雨的下午，我们按预约参观了那个小型服装收藏馆。
by birth	prepositional phrase	按血统；生来	The novel's hero is a prince by birth but grows up among travelling actors.	小说主人公生来是王子，却在巡回演出的演员中长大。
by comparison with	prepositional phrase	与…相比	By comparison with the draughty attic, the tiny kitchen felt wonderfully warm.	与漏风的阁楼相比，小厨房显得暖和极了。
by contrast	prepositional phrase	相比之下	The first sketch was crowded with detail; the second, by contrast, used only a few lines.	第一张素描细节繁多；相比之下，第二张只用了寥寥几笔。
by courtesy of	prepositional phrase	承蒙…的好意	We borrowed a rehearsal room by courtesy of the village school.	承蒙村里学校的好意，我们借到了一间排练室。
by default	prepositional phrase	因对手缺席而	Our team won by default when the other players failed to appear.	对方队员没有到场，我们队因此不战而胜。
by degrees	prepositional phrase	逐渐地	By degrees, the muddy water in the jar became clear.	罐子里的泥水渐渐变清了。
by dint of	preposition	凭借	By dint of patient practice, Theo learned to balance the tray on one hand.	凭借耐心练习，西奥学会了用一只手平稳地托住托盘。

by fair means or foul	prepositional phrase	不择手段地	The villain intends to obtain the missing jewel by fair means or foul.	反派打算不择手段地弄到那颗失踪的宝石。
by force of	preposition	由于；凭借	By force of habit, I reached for a light switch that was no longer there.	出于习惯，我伸手去摸一个早已不在那里的电灯开关。
by half	prepositional phrase	太；过分	His excuse was too elaborate by half to sound convincing.	他的借口编得太复杂，反而显得不可信。
by law	prepositional phrase	根据法律	In the story, every household must keep a lantern by law.	故事中，法律规定每户人家都必须备有一盏灯。
by means of	preposition	借助；依靠	We lifted the heavy lid by means of a rope threaded through its handle.	我们借助一根穿过把手的绳子抬起了沉重的盖子。
by no manner of means	prepositional phrase	决不；绝非	The first attempt was by no manner of means a complete failure.	第一次尝试绝非彻底失败。
by reason of	preposition	由于〔正式用语〕	The old chest was difficult to move by reason of its enormous weight.	那只旧箱子十分沉重，因此很难搬动。
by reputation	prepositional phrase	凭名声	I knew the violin maker by reputation before visiting her crowded workshop.	在拜访那位制琴师拥挤的工作室之前，我已听说过她的名声。
by the name of	prepositional phrase	名叫	A gardener by the name of Ellis helped us identify the damaged tree.	一位名叫埃利斯的园丁帮我们辨认了那棵受损的树。
by the same token	prepositional phrase	出于同样的原因	A larger sail catches more wind; by the same token, it is harder to control.	更大的帆能兜住更多的风；出于同样的原因，它也更难控制。
by turns	prepositional phrase	交替地	The story was by turns funny and unsettling, keeping us awake long after midnight.	这个故事时而好笑，时而令人不安，让我们过了午夜很久仍睡不着。
by virtue of	preposition	由于；凭借	She could reach the top shelf by virtue of her height.	由于个子高，她够得着最上面的架子。
care of	preposition	由…转交	Send the parcel to me care of my elder sister while I am away.	我不在时，请把包裹寄给我姐姐，由她转交给我。
compared to	prepositional phrase	与…相比	Compared to our old tent, this one feels like a palace.	与我们的旧帐篷相比，这顶简直像座宫殿。
compared with	preposition	与…相比	The blue fabric feels rough compared with the green sample.	与绿色样品相比，蓝色布料摸起来很粗糙。
complete with	preposition	连同；包括	The children built a cardboard castle, complete with a drawbridge and a tiny flag.	孩子们用纸板做了一座城堡，还配上了吊桥和一面小旗。
concerning	preposition	关于	I found a handwritten note concerning the missing violin inside the empty case.	我在空琴盒里发现了一张关于失踪小提琴的手写便条。
considering	preposition	就…而言；考虑到	Considering the narrow doorway, we were lucky to get the sofa inside.	考虑到门口那么窄，我们能把沙发搬进去已经很幸运了。
contrary to	preposition	与…相反	Contrary to my expectations, the repaired clock ran quietly all night.	与我的预期相反，修好的钟整夜都安静地走着。
down the drain	prepositional phrase	被浪费掉	All that careful rehearsal went down the drain when we forgot the costumes.	我们忘带了服装，之前精心进行的排练全都白费了。
down the line	prepositional phrase	完全地；处处〔非正式用语〕	The committee rejected our proposal right down the line, from its budget to its design.	委员会把我们的提案从预算到设计全盘否决了。
down to	preposition	一直到；下至	She checked every part of the costume, down to the smallest button.	她检查了服装的每个部分，连最小的纽扣也没有放过。
due to	preposition	由于	The delay was due to a missing key, not a broken lock.	延误是因为钥匙不见了，而不是锁坏了。
except for	preposition	除了…之外	The stage was empty except for a single chair beneath the spotlight.	舞台上空无一物，只有聚光灯下的一把椅子。
excepting	preposition	除…之外	Excepting the heavy oak table, we moved every piece of furniture upstairs.	除了那张沉重的橡木桌，我们把所有家具都搬到了楼上。
excluding	preposition	不包括	The tour lasted three hours, excluding the time we spent waiting for the bus.	这次游览持续了三个小时，不包括我们等公交车的时间。
for a change	prepositional phrase	换换口味；改变一下	Let's eat outside for a change instead of squeezing into the kitchen.	我们换个地方到外面吃吧，别再挤在厨房里了。
for all	prepositional phrase	尽管	For all his confidence, the young actor kept checking the script.	尽管那位年轻演员很自信，他仍不停地查看剧本。
for better or worse	prepositional phrase	不论好坏	For better or worse, we have painted the entire kitchen purple.	不论结果好坏，我们已经把整个厨房刷成紫色了。
for fear of	preposition	唯恐；生怕	She carried the cracked bowl in both hands for fear of dropping it.	她生怕把那只裂了的碗摔下去，便用双手端着。
for hire	prepositional phrase	供出租	A row of small boats for hire rocked gently beside the wooden pier.	一排供出租的小船在木码头旁轻轻摇晃。
for laughs	prepositional phrase	为了开心；闹着玩	We wore matching paper crowns for laughs during the long train journey.	长途坐火车时，我们为了逗乐，戴上了款式相同的纸王冠。
for my part	prepositional phrase	就我而言	For my part, I would rather repair the old chairs than replace them.	就我而言，我宁愿修好那些旧椅子，也不愿换掉它们。
for one thing	prepositional phrase	首先；一来	We cannot rehearse here; for one thing, the ceiling is too low.	我们不能在这里排练；首先，天花板就太低了。
for size	prepositional phrase	为试尺码	The customer tried the riding boots for size before asking about their price.	顾客先试了试那双马靴的尺码，然后才询问价格。
for the benefit of	prepositional phrase	为了…的利益	We kept the main garden path clear for the benefit of visitors with pushchairs.	为了方便推婴儿车的游客，我们让花园里的主路保持畅通。
for the best	prepositional phrase	出于好意	She meant it for the best when she secretly repaired his battered hat.	她偷偷修补他那顶破旧的帽子，本是出于好意。
for the better	prepositional phrase	向好的方面；有所改善	The mood in the workshop changed for the better after the missing tools turned up.	失踪的工具找到后，工作间里的气氛好转了。
for the last time	prepositional phrase	最后一次	He checked the empty cupboard for the last time before returning the keys.	交还钥匙前，他最后检查了一次空橱柜。
for the present	prepositional phrase	暂时	For the present, we are keeping the spare costumes in the dining room.	我们暂时把备用服装放在餐厅里。
for the record	prepositional phrase	供记录；备案	The chair asked everyone to state their name for the record before the meeting began.	会议开始前，主持人请大家报上姓名，以便记录。
for the sake of	prepositional phrase	为了…起见	We left the door unlocked for the sake of the late arrivals.	为了方便迟到的人，我们没有锁门。
for the worse	prepositional phrase	向坏的方面；恶化	The weather took a turn for the worse just as we unfolded the picnic blanket.	我们刚展开野餐毯，天气就变坏了。
for want of	preposition	由于缺乏	The half-built puppet lay unfinished for want of a suitable piece of cloth.	由于缺少合适的布料，那只做了一半的木偶还没有完成。
from a distance	prepositional phrase	从远处	From a distance, the sheep on the hillside looked like scattered stones.	从远处看，山坡上的羊就像散落的石头。
from all accounts	prepositional phrase	据大家所说	From all accounts, the new caretaker can repair almost anything in the building.	据大家所说，新管理员几乎能修好楼里的任何东西。
from force of habit	prepositional phrase	出于习惯	From force of habit, she folded the newspaper before handing it to me.	出于习惯，她先把报纸折起来，再递给我。
from memory	prepositional phrase	凭记忆	I drew the old garden from memory and forgot the little shed.	我凭记忆画出了那座旧花园，却忘了那个小棚子。
from side to side	prepositional phrase	左右地	The lamp swung from side to side as the carriage crossed the uneven bridge.	马车驶过凹凸不平的桥面时，灯左右摇摆。
from stem to stern	prepositional phrase	从头到尾；彻底地	The crew scrubbed the little boat from stem to stern before the visitors arrived.	访客到来前，船员们把小船从船头到船尾彻底擦洗了一遍。
from the cradle to the grave	prepositional phrase	从生到死；一辈子	The novel follows its restless heroine from the cradle to the grave.	这部小说讲述了那位不安于现状的女主人公从出生到去世的一生。
from the outset	prepositional phrase	从一开始	From the outset, I knew the huge wardrobe would not fit through our door.	从一开始，我就知道那个大衣柜过不了我们家的门。
from time immemorial	prepositional phrase	自古以来	In the tale, villagers have guarded the mysterious well from time immemorial.	故事中，村民们自古以来就守护着那口神秘的井。
from top to bottom	prepositional phrase	从上到下；完完全全	We searched the cupboard from top to bottom without finding the missing cup.	我们把橱柜从上到下找了个遍，却没找到丢失的杯子。
from top to toe	prepositional phrase	从头到脚	After crawling beneath the stage, Sam was covered in dust from top to toe.	从舞台底下爬过之后，萨姆从头到脚都是灰。
hand in glove with	prepositional phrase	与…勾结	In the detective story, the hotel manager works hand in glove with the jewel thieves.	侦探故事中，旅馆经理与珠宝窃贼相互勾结。
in a big way	prepositional phrase	大规模地；彻底地	The family celebrated the shop's anniversary in a big way, inviting the whole street.	那家人大张旗鼓地庆祝商店周年，邀请了整条街的人。
in a cleft stick	prepositional phrase	进退两难〔英式用语〕	Promising the same room to two visitors left the host in a cleft stick.	主人把同一间房许给了两位访客，结果陷入了两难。
in a huff	prepositional phrase	怒气冲冲地	She left in a huff after we laughed at her enormous umbrella.	我们嘲笑她那把硕大的雨伞，她便气冲冲地走了。
in a jiffy	prepositional phrase	马上；立刻〔非正式用语〕	I'll fetch a clean towel and be back in a jiffy.	我去拿条干净毛巾，马上就回来。
in a manner of speaking	prepositional phrase	不妨说；可以说	The garden became our classroom, in a manner of speaking, during the painting course.	可以说，上绘画课期间，那座花园成了我们的教室。
in a pinch	prepositional phrase	必要时；在紧要关头〔美式用语〕	In a pinch, a folded blanket can serve as a seat cushion.	必要时，折起来的毯子可以当坐垫用。
in a row	prepositional phrase	连续地	The drummer dropped a stick three times in a row during rehearsal.	排练时，鼓手接连三次掉了鼓槌。
in a sense	prepositional phrase	在某种意义上	In a sense, repairing the old boat brought the whole family together again.	从某种意义上说，修理旧船让全家人又团结到了一起。
in a state	prepositional phrase	焦躁不安〔非正式用语〕	He was in a state after discovering that his passport was missing.	他发现护照不见后，急得不知如何是好。
in a stew	prepositional phrase	焦急；烦恼〔非正式用语〕	Maya was in a stew about the cake she had forgotten to collect.	玛雅忘了去取蛋糕，正为此发愁。
in a sweat	prepositional phrase	一身大汗	The porter arrived in a sweat after carrying our cases up four flights of stairs.	搬运工提着我们的箱子爬了四段楼梯，来到时已是一身大汗。

on the increase	prepositional phrase	正在增长	Attendance at the evening classes is on the increase, so we need another room.	晚间课程的出席人数正在增加，所以我们还需要一间教室。

on the make	prepositional phrase	野心勃勃的	The novel follows a young salesman on the make who treats every friendship as a business opportunity.	小说讲述一个野心勃勃的年轻推销员，他把每段友谊都当成做生意的机会。
on the map	prepositional phrase	出名的；受到重视的	The successful film festival put the small seaside town on the map.	那次成功的电影节让这座海滨小镇出了名。

on the market	prepositional phrase	待售的	The house had been on the market for months before anyone arranged a viewing.	那栋房子挂牌出售好几个月后，才有人预约看房。
on the mend	prepositional phrase	在好转中	My ankle is on the mend, though I still avoid the steep path home.	我的脚踝正在好转，不过我回家时仍然避开那条陡路。

on the phone	prepositional phrase	在打电话	I couldn't answer the door because I was on the phone to the repair shop.	我当时正在给维修店打电话，所以没法去开门。
on the point of	preposition	正要……的时候	We were on the point of leaving when the missing keys turned up.	我们正要出发时，那串找不到的钥匙出现了。
on the prowl	prepositional phrase	四出寻觅	The cat was on the prowl again, peering behind every flowerpot in the garden.	那只猫又在四处搜寻，朝花园里每个花盆后面张望。
on the rack	prepositional phrase	焦虑不安；受折磨	The long silence kept her on the rack while she waited for news of the missing boat.	等待失踪小船的消息时，长时间没有音信让她备受煎熬。
on the rampage	prepositional phrase	横冲直撞；肆意破坏	In the cartoon, a robot goes on the rampage and knocks over the market stalls.	在那部动画片里，一个机器人横冲直撞，撞翻了市场上的摊位。
on the right track	prepositional phrase	方向正确的	The first few correct answers suggested that our new approach was on the right track.	最初几道题答对了，这说明我们的新方法方向是对的。
on the rocks	prepositional phrase	触礁的	The storm left the fishing boat on the rocks below the empty lighthouse.	风暴过后，渔船搁在那座空无人烟的灯塔下方的礁石上。
on the ropes	prepositional phrase	濒于失败的；处于困境的	With two major orders cancelled, the little furniture business was on the ropes.	两笔大订单被取消后，那家小家具企业濒临倒闭。
on the run	prepositional phrase	在逃的	In the film, the thieves remain on the run after abandoning their broken van.	在那部电影里，窃贼丢下坏掉的货车后仍然在逃。
on the scene	prepositional phrase	在事发现场	A neighbour was already on the scene when the first fire engine arrived.	第一辆消防车到达时，一位邻居已经在事发现场了。
on the shelf	prepositional phrase	被搁置的	The plan stayed on the shelf because nobody could find the money to fund it.	因为没人能找到资金，那项计划一直被搁置着。
on the strength of	preposition	凭借；依据	We hired the carpenter on the strength of a neighbour's recommendation.	我们根据一位邻居的推荐雇用了那名木匠。
on the telephone	prepositional phrase	在通电话	She spent an hour on the telephone trying to arrange a replacement delivery.	她打了一个小时的电话，试图安排重新送货。
on the town	prepositional phrase	在城里寻欢作乐	We planned a night on the town, starting with dinner and ending at a dance club.	我们计划进城玩一晚，先吃晚饭，最后去一家舞蹈俱乐部。
on the trot	prepositional phrase	接连地	Our little team won three games on the trot before finally losing to the visitors.	我们的小队连赢了三场，最后才输给客队。
on the verge of	preposition	濒临；眼看就要	The old bridge was on the verge of collapse, so the path was closed.	那座旧桥眼看就要坍塌，因此小路被封闭了。
on the wagon	prepositional phrase	戒酒的	I'm on the wagon this month, so I'll have sparkling water with dinner.	我这个月戒酒，所以晚饭时喝气泡水。
on the warpath	prepositional phrase	非常气愤的	The supervisor was on the warpath after finding paint spilled across the new carpet.	主管发现新地毯上洒满了颜料，气得大发雷霆。
on the way out	prepositional phrase	即将消亡；即将被淘汰	The old paper timetable is on the way out as more passengers use the app.	越来越多的乘客使用应用程序，那种旧式纸质时刻表即将被淘汰。
on the wrong side of	prepositional phrase	已过……岁	I'm on the wrong side of forty, but I still enjoy learning a new dance.	我已过四十岁，不过仍然喜欢学一种新的舞蹈。
on the wrong track	prepositional phrase	方向不对的	We realised we were on the wrong track when the figures stopped matching the receipts.	当数字开始与收据对不上时，我们意识到思路错了。
on tiptoe	prepositional phrase	踮着脚尖	I stood on tiptoe to reach the last mug on the highest shelf.	我踮起脚尖，去够最高一层架子上的最后一只马克杯。
on tiptoes	prepositional phrase	踮着脚尖	The children crept on tiptoes past the room where the baby was sleeping.	孩子们踮着脚尖，悄悄走过婴儿正在睡觉的房间。
on top of	preposition	在……上面	Someone had left a wet umbrella on top of my carefully folded coat.	有人把一把湿伞放在了我仔细叠好的外套上。
on top of the world	prepositional phrase	幸福到极点的	I felt on top of the world when my older sister finally came home.	姐姐终于回家时，我觉得幸福极了。
on track	prepositional phrase	未偏离目标；进展正常	The revised schedule kept the building project on track despite a week of rain.	虽然下了一周的雨，调整后的日程仍使建筑项目按目标推进。
on view	prepositional phrase	正在展览的	Several sketches are on view beside the artist's finished paintings.	艺术家的成品画旁边正在展出几幅素描。
on watch	prepositional phrase	在值班	The sailor on watch noticed a light flashing beyond the harbour wall.	值班水手注意到港口防波堤外有一盏灯在闪烁。
one and the same	pronoun	同一个	The anonymous donor and our former neighbour turned out to be one and the same.	那位匿名捐赠者原来就是我们以前的邻居。
other than	preposition	除了	The cupboard held nothing other than a cracked bowl and a bag of rice.	橱柜里除了一只裂碗和一袋米，什么也没有。
out of action	prepositional phrase	停止运转；无法使用	The lift was out of action, so we carried the boxes up four flights of stairs.	电梯不能用了，我们只好把箱子搬上四段楼梯。
out of breath	prepositional phrase	上气不接下气	I reached the platform out of breath just as the train doors opened.	火车门刚打开，我就气喘吁吁地赶到了站台。
out of character	prepositional phrase	不符合一贯性格的	It was out of character for him to leave without saying goodbye.	不告而别不像他一贯的作风。
out of commission	prepositional phrase	不能使用的	A damaged cable left the old projector out of commission for the whole weekend.	一根损坏的电缆让旧投影仪整个周末都无法使用。
out of condition	prepositional phrase	身体状况不佳的	After months without exercise, I felt out of condition on the first hill.	几个月没有锻炼，刚爬第一座小山我就觉得体能不行了。
out of control	prepositional phrase	失去控制	The shopping trolley rolled out of control down the sloping car park.	购物车失控地顺着倾斜的停车场滑了下去。
out of danger	prepositional phrase	脱离危险	The hikers were out of danger once they reached the shelter above the rising water.	徒步者到了上涨水位上方的避难处后，就脱离了危险。
out of focus	prepositional phrase	焦点未对准的；模糊的	The background was clear, but every face in the photograph was out of focus.	照片的背景很清楚，可每张脸都没有对上焦。
out of joint	prepositional phrase	脱节的；脱臼的	The wooden puppet's knee was out of joint, so one leg hung at an odd angle.	木偶的膝关节脱节了，因此一条腿以奇怪的角度垂着。
out of keeping with	prepositional phrase	与……不一致	The bright plastic sign looked out of keeping with the quiet stone courtyard.	那块鲜艳的塑料招牌看起来与安静的石砌庭院很不协调。
out of kilter	prepositional phrase	不正常；出了毛病	The new shift pattern threw our household routine out of kilter.	新的轮班安排打乱了我们家的日常作息。
out of line	prepositional phrase	不成直线的	One tile was out of line with the others along the kitchen wall.	厨房墙上有一块瓷砖没有与其他瓷砖排齐。
out of proportion	prepositional phrase	不成比例的	The model's tiny wheels looked out of proportion to its enormous body.	模型的轮子很小，与庞大的车身不成比例。
out of service	prepositional phrase	失效；不能使用	The automatic door was out of service after its sensor failed.	传感器失灵后，那扇自动门就不能使用了。
out of shape	prepositional phrase	变形的	The lid had bent out of shape and would no longer fit the tin.	盖子已经弯曲变形，再也盖不上那个铁罐了。
out of step	prepositional phrase	步调不一致的	I kept marching out of step until I started listening to the drum.	开始留意鼓声之前，我行进的步伐总是不合拍。
out of step with	prepositional phrase	与……不协调	The proposal seemed out of step with what residents had asked for at the meeting.	那项提议似乎与居民在会上提出的要求不一致。
out of sync	prepositional phrase	不同步的	The subtitles were out of sync with the video after I changed the playback speed.	我改变播放速度后，字幕就与视频不同步了。
out of the picture	prepositional phrase	不相干；不再相关	Once we decided to walk, parking fees were out of the picture.	一旦决定步行，停车费就与我们的安排无关了。
out of touch with	prepositional phrase	对……不了解；脱离……	The manager seemed out of touch with the problems faced by staff on the night shift.	经理似乎不了解夜班员工面临的问题。
out of tune	prepositional phrase	走调的	The violin was so badly out of tune that we stopped the rehearsal.	那把小提琴走调得太厉害，我们只好停止排练。
out of use	prepositional phrase	不再使用的；废弃的	The old drinking fountain has been out of use since the pipes were removed.	水管被拆除后，那座旧饮水喷泉就一直没有再使用。
over the counter	prepositional phrase	无需处方购买	She asked the pharmacist whether the cream was sold over the counter.	她问药剂师，那种乳膏是否无需处方就能购买。
over the hill	prepositional phrase	过了巅峰期的；在衰退中的	The singer refused to believe he was over the hill and began rehearsing for another tour.	那位歌手不肯相信自己已过巅峰期，又开始为下一轮巡演排练。
over the hump	prepositional phrase	度过最困难时期的	With the roof repaired and the walls dry, we felt we were over the hump.	屋顶修好、墙壁干透后，我们觉得最困难的阶段已经过去了。
over the moon	prepositional phrase	兴高采烈的	The children were over the moon when we told them about the camping trip.	听我们说起那次露营旅行，孩子们高兴极了。
owing to	preposition	由于	Owing to a broken water pipe, the café could serve only cold drinks that morning.	由于水管破裂，那天早晨咖啡馆只能供应冷饮。
preparatory to	prepositional phrase	作为……的准备	We moved the furniture into the hall preparatory to painting the sitting room.	为了准备粉刷客厅，我们把家具搬进了门厅。
prior to	preposition	在……之前	Please check the address prior to posting the parcel, especially the apartment number.	寄包裹前请核对地址，尤其是公寓号码。
pursuant to	prepositional phrase	依照；按照	Pursuant to the club's rules, the secretary sent every member notice of the meeting.	依照俱乐部的规则，秘书向每位会员发出了会议通知。
rather than	preposition	而不是；与其……不如……	We chose a small table rather than a sofa for the narrow balcony.	我们给狭窄的阳台选了一张小桌子，而不是沙发。
regarding	preposition	关于	I left a message regarding the missing parcel and asked someone to call me back.	我就丢失的包裹留了言，请对方回电话。
regardless of	preposition	不顾；不关心	He kept buying new equipment regardless of the shop's mounting debts.	他不顾店里不断增加的债务，继续购买新设备。
right off the bat	prepositional phrase	马上；一下子	Right off the bat, she noticed that the two totals did not match.	她一下子就注意到两个总数对不上。
since time immemorial	prepositional phrase	自古以来	In the folktale, the villagers have gathered beside the great oak since time immemorial.	在那则民间故事中，村民们自古以来就聚集在那棵大橡树旁。
subsequent to	prepositional phrase	在……之后	Subsequent to the inspection, the owner replaced the broken window and repaired the gate.	检查之后，业主更换了破窗，并修好了大门。
thanks to	preposition	由于；多亏	Thanks to a neighbour's spare key, we got inside before the rain began.	多亏邻居有一把备用钥匙，我们在下雨前进了屋。
this and that	pronoun	各种各样的东西；这个那个	We spent the afternoon sorting this and that from the boxes in the attic.	我们花了一个下午，整理阁楼箱子里的各种东西。
to a large extent	prepositional phrase	在很大程度上	The success of the fair depended to a large extent on the volunteers' careful planning.	集市的成功在很大程度上依赖志愿者的周密筹划。
to a tee	prepositional phrase	恰好；完全符合地	The description fits our old kitchen to a tee, even down to the cracked blue tiles.	那段描写与我们的旧厨房完全吻合，连裂开的蓝瓷砖都一样。
to all appearances	prepositional phrase	就外表来看	To all appearances, the suitcase was empty, but a letter lay under the lining.	从外表看，行李箱是空的，不过衬里下面藏着一封信。
to bits	prepositional phrase	成碎片	The fallen branch smashed the little wooden bench to bits.	掉下来的树枝把那张小木凳砸得粉碎。
to death	prepositional phrase	极度地	I'm bored to death with this endless argument about where to put the cupboard.	关于柜子该放在哪里的争论没完没了，我烦透了。
to distraction	prepositional phrase	到心烦意乱的程度	The dripping tap drove me to distraction while I tried to finish the letter.	我想把信写完时，水龙头不断滴水，弄得我心烦意乱。
to hand	prepositional phrase	在手头	Keep a notebook to hand so you can write down the measurements immediately.	把笔记本放在手边，这样就能立即记下测量结果。
to no avail	prepositional phrase	完全无用；徒劳地	We searched every drawer to no avail; the receipt was still missing.	我们翻遍了每个抽屉，还是白费力气；收据仍然找不到。
to pieces	prepositional phrase	成碎片	The old cardboard box fell to pieces when I tried to lift it.	我试着搬起那个旧纸箱时，它散成了碎片。
to scale	prepositional phrase	按比例缩小	The architect drew the garden to scale so we could see how the new path would fit.	建筑师按比例缩小画出花园，让我们能看出新小路将如何布局。
to some degree	prepositional phrase	在某种程度上	We all felt responsible to some degree for leaving the gate open.	对于没有关大门这件事，我们大家都觉得自己多少有些责任。
to some extent	prepositional phrase	在某种程度上	The thicker curtains reduced the noise to some extent, but we could still hear the traffic.	较厚的窗帘在一定程度上减轻了噪声，不过我们仍能听见车流声。
to taste	prepositional phrase	按口味	Stir the lemon juice into the dressing, then add a little pepper to taste.	把柠檬汁拌入调味汁，再按口味加少许胡椒。
to the bitter end	prepositional phrase	坚持到底	Even when the score looked hopeless, the team kept fighting to the bitter end.	即使比分已经让人绝望，球队仍然拼到了最后。
to the bone	prepositional phrase	到极点；彻底地	We were chilled to the bone after waiting for the bus in the icy wind.	在刺骨的寒风中等公交车后，我们冷得透骨。
to the core	prepositional phrase	直至核心	The apple was rotten to the core, although its skin still looked smooth.	那只苹果已经烂到果核，尽管外皮看起来还很光滑。
to the detriment of	prepositional phrase	有损于；对……不利	The company cut cleaning hours to the detriment of everyone who used the building.	公司缩短了清洁工时，使所有使用那栋楼的人都受到不利影响。
to the end of time	prepositional phrase	永远	In the song, the sailor promises to remember his hometown to the end of time.	在那首歌里，水手许诺永远记住自己的家乡。
to the exclusion of	preposition	排斥；不顾	She focused on the border pattern to the exclusion of every other detail in the painting.	她只顾看画中的边框图案，忽略了所有其他细节。
to the extent of	prepositional phrase	达到……程度	The storm damaged the roof to the extent of exposing the wooden rafters.	风暴把屋顶损坏到了露出木椽的程度。
to the fore	prepositional phrase	到前面	During the parade, the drummers moved to the fore and led the procession.	游行时，鼓手们走到了前面，领着队伍前进。
to the last	prepositional phrase	到底；直至最后	She stayed loyal to the little theatre to the last, even when its audience dwindled.	即使观众越来越少，她也始终支持那家小剧院。

reviewAudit.limitation: Identity and exact input binding are mechanically checked; genuine language reading is an accountable human/AI-reader assertion, not inferred from hashes.

authorDeferrals.reason: The sole published Chinese is the chemistry-tagged 不计价. The personally read Collins entry instead makes a trial offer conditional on trying and being satisfied before paying; its thesaurus also lists free, but that does not establish this particular chemistry sense or unrestricted no-charge meaning. I have not composed a pair by silently replacing the published sense with no obligation to purchase.

Published meaning 一...就 requires the temporal conjunction use in a natural clause. This queue currently permits only preposition from its mixed preposition/conjunction source. I will not label a conjunction example preposition or silently expand the enabled POS contract.

The only source Chinese is 加州葡萄. Personally read Collins distinguishes Pinot grape varieties from their wines and does not identify Pinot with California grapes generally. The frozen Chinese is too geographically broad/underspecified to select a reliable equivalent without a finite source-sense decision; no wine sense or silently repaired 皮诺葡萄 label is substituted here.

The frozen noun gloss and variant only transliterate 蒙特苏马, without specifying which person or other named referent. I have not selected a ruler, place, or fictional random namesake by capitalization/familiarity alone.

The entire Chinese genus gloss is corrupted as Ы鱼属, with a Cyrillic character in place of its identifying Chinese text. I have not silently repaired it to 鲟鱼属 or used the adjacent Acipenseridae source as authority to rewrite this head's source.

Frozen Chinese is solely 秋水仙碱, a chemical sense. Personally read Kew records exact Acroclinium as a botanical synonym associated with Rhodanthe, not evidence for that chemical identity. A plant sentence would change the published sense; a colchicine sentence would assert an unsupported English head/chemical mapping.

The source begins with corrupted ǎ蕨属 and gives 金蕨属 in parentheses. The personally read original Flora of China identifies genus 卤蕨属 and 金蕨 as a species alias for Acrostichum aureum, not clear evidence for the frozen genus-level 金蕨属 equivalence. I am not upgrading a species alias to the genus or silently repairing the corrupted first label.

The source is 肉珊瑚目. Personally read Merriam-Webster treats exact Actinaria as a synonym of Actiniaria, but I have not established that the frozen Chinese denotes this same historical order rather than another coral grouping. I have not substituted the neighbouring head's 海葵目 label or pronounced the old head invalid.

Frozen Chinese 凤尾蕨属 is not the exact genus mapping found in personally read original iPlant, which gives 眉刷蕨属; Kew confirms the exact English genus. Different preferred names alone do not prove that every historical alias is wrong, but no primary evidence closed this particular alias. A limited source-mapping hold is safer than silently replacing the Chinese genus.

The sole frozen gloss is the malformed 构成鹫科. The initial verb 构成 is not a usable noun meaning and the intended historical family boundaries have not been independently resolved. I have not simply deleted that text and asserted an exact modern family mapping.

Frozen Chinese 山楂 denotes hawthorn, while this Latin-looking zoological head has no source evidence tying it to that plant. I have not changed the spelling or replaced the Chinese with an inferred elephant-bird order. This specific head/gloss conflict needs source repair or a separately bound decision, not a fabricated plant example.

authorDeferrals.reason: Frozen medical senses combine reversed direction with passivation/reactivation. The indexed 1951 tooth-paper title establishes another dental context but not either exact Chinese branch. No exact original definition was read closing this selected medical sense; do not borrow the familiar rhetorical anastrophe meaning.

Frozen 四硫双羟乙酸钠盐 is a precise chemical identity, not enough to verify whether this exact old name denotes a compound or a preparation. Original bounded head lookup did not resolve its composition; a neutral vial sentence would only conceal the unresolved identity.

Frozen adjective conflates muscle regeneration with nourishment. The similarly spelled anatreptic is a different word; the bounded original head search did not close anathreptic and the selected Chinese branch. Do not infer a muscle-regenerating claim from the suffix.

Frozen 失仪症 is a medical behavioural label. The original Century head actually read instead gives incongruous arrangement, specifically in art. This does not validate the frozen medical branch, so neither an artistic example nor an invented diagnosis can be substituted silently.

The precise frozen diphtheria-toxoid sensitivity test requires exact historical test identity; no original head passage was located in the finite lookup. Do not infer a testing procedure or equate it with general toxoid reaction.

Frozen allowed role is adjective but its only Chinese sense 揉擦剂 is a remedy noun. The original Stedman passage actually read likewise defines a remedy applied by friction/inunction. A finite role/sense repair is required before a source-compatible sentence.

Original Stedman actually read gives nourishing and preventing/curing atrophy. Frozen 防衰 may be read as anti-ageing, which is not the precise atrophy concept. Do not publish an anti-ageing property or silently replace the selected Chinese with a materially narrower medical definition.

Frozen upward-latent-squint adjective could be confused with botanical anatropous and the general upturned sense. Original Stedman read confirms related noun anatropia, not this exact adjective, while the original terminology result was Catalan, not proof of English spelling/role. Exact English medical adjective remains for finite verification.

Frozen 听觉缺失 is hearing loss; this head is associated with speech/voice loss, not deafness. The finite primary lookup did not close the exact original head, so the hearing/speech conflict must be resolved before any example rather than reinforce the frozen mismatch.

Frozen 癔病喉痉挛 is a historical diagnostic/causal formulation. Exact original head and historical scope were not resolved by the finite search; avoid teaching a modern psychogenic diagnosis or inferring causation from an undifferentiated throat symptom.

Frozen role is adjective, whereas both original Century and Stedman passages actually read express the direction toward the elbow. A movement sentence would use a directional adverb; converting it into an elbow-related adjective would silently change the frozen role/sense.

Exact frozen family spelling has -astom- rather than the separately queued Ancylostomatidae. The bounded original search did not verify the variant as a historical taxonomic name. Do not silently normalize the letters or teach it as an accepted family spelling.

Frozen hookworm-disease spelling has -astom- rather than the familiar -ostom-. An original exact-head variant reference is still needed; neither an assumed typo correction nor familiarity with hookworm disease verifies this written form.

Frozen exact genus spelling differs from independently queued Ancylostoma. The finite original lookup did not establish this as a taxonomic synonym or historical genus. Must close that precise naming status rather than infer it from shared hookworm Chinese.

Frozen sole role/sense is a person noun 安达曼人, whereas the original Century window read contains Andaman only inside the separate Andamanese entry. It does not establish a count-person use of bare Andaman. Place-name usage would not match the frozen person branch.

Frozen ethnonym omits an internal a compared with Andamanese. The exact spelling is not closed by an original source; do not disguise an unverified ethnonym in a quoted label or silently use the conventional form.

Frozen ovarian male-cell-tumour term differs from independently queued androblastoma/andreioma. Exact historical head identity remains unresolved; an archive-report sentence would not establish whether this is a recognized variant or a transcription problem.

Frozen medical 精子细胞 may refer to a spermatid, but the exact cell type and domain need original verification, especially against botanical male-cell usage. No exact original head was found in the bounded lookup; do not infer a mammalian cell identity from the components.

Frozen 羊踯躅毒素 resembles the separately queued andromedotoxin family but the exact head has unusual -dedotaxin spelling. Original chemical identity/spelling was not closed; do not silently replace it or manufacture a compound example.

Frozen [机] 雄茸属 has a domain/Chinese-identity problem. A primary botanical key indexed this exact spelling, but that does not establish this Chinese taxon or its relation to Andrographis. Need source reconciliation rather than choose a familiar plant genus silently.

Original Century head actually read combines historical androgyny/bisexuality/hermaphroditism, while frozen medical branches conflate anatomy with feminization and outdated classifications. Original Stedman head actually read is a historical person noun for hermaphrodite. Frozen multiple branches include feminized men and intersex traits without distinction. A finite historically framed selected-sense/status clarification is required before teaching a learner-facing person label.

Frozen 雄甾酮 does not independently verify this exact old chemical/trade name. No original head passage was read closing androkin versus androsterone or a preparation; do not assert identity through a generic container sentence.

Frozen dwarf-name spelling differs from common Andvari, but no original exact mythological head was read establishing this variant. Must verify the name before presenting it as a character; do not declare it invalid merely from no search match.

perTerm.reason: The cheese maker uses the source plant-derived colourant to colour a mixture orange. Independently read manufacturer text supports that actual cheese-colouring application; no dose, safety or recipe instruction is given.
Glass bowls cooling overnight inside a furnace naturally select the published 退火炉 noun branch, not the medical instrument; duration and falling temperature are faithfully translated.
A fictional group's last afternoon in the explicitly sourced French city is spent looking for a gift; the place role and continuing search match Chinese without geographic invention.

The English says her sister, without saying older or younger; Chinese 姐姐 specifies an older sister. The source female-name role and ordinary scene are sound, but the unsupported kinship age needs a separately source-bound translation amendment, not an edit to the frozen evidence.
The explicitly sourced female given name refers to a fictional person bringing a folding chair because seats are scarce; Chinese preserves the reason and chair without an added biography.
A letter from the sourced American city arrives two days before its writer comes home for the holidays; location, timing and the returning person's identity align.

The actual reaction scheme includes construction of an additional ring, a concrete chemical-process noun use consistent with the independently read original IUPAC entry; the Chinese keeps the second-ring statement.
Numbering the carbon atoms of a depicted annulene before discussing its structure is a natural educational use of the source hydrocarbon class, without falsely fixing every annulene's ring size.

Panels undergo the source surface-treatment process before their protective covering is removed; the past production scene and ordering are faithfully translated, with no general procedure or performance claim.
Sampling the anode electrolyte separately from cathode-compartment liquid realizes 阳极电解液 and preserves the stated intention to avoid mixing rather than an invented result.

One illustrated sugar configuration has its hydroxyl group drawn downwards, compatible with the independently read anomer identity; the sentence does not claim all sugars or anomers share that orientation.
Following a changing ratio of two sugar forms is a genuine interconversion-process use; selected 端基异构化 is the same chemical identity as the source older 正位异构化 wording, not a new unrelated reaction.

The English my cousin leaves sex, relative age and paternal-versus-maternal cousin branch unspecified. Chinese 表弟 adds all of male/younger/表 rather than 堂. Keep this immutable row review-held pending a bounded amendment; the Anqing place identity itself is sound.

A proposed linear form is tried and checked against a differential equation, an actual mathematical 拟设 rather than a definition or mention-only filler; Chinese preserves the check sequence and uncertainty.

English my grandmother does not identify paternal versus maternal lineage, but Chinese 我祖母 fixes the paternal side. The city's source identity and exhibition scene are sound; a separately bound kinship precision amendment is needed before this row can count.
Leaving a winter coat in the explicitly sourced city leads to borrowing one for a journey; Chinese retains the place, necessity and clothing relation without extra geography.
The source mythological giant is depicted in a sculptor's imagined wrestling composition, not asserted as a historical event or an arbitrary real-name bearer; the Chinese image placement aligns.
The adjective modifies muscles in an educational forearm drawing between elbow and wrist, matching 前臂的 rather than 上臂 and keeping the visual-reference context.
A student marks the forearm on a model and then points to the upper arm; the two distinct body regions and subsequent action are translated correctly.
The diagram's uterine body bends forward relative to its cervix, consistent with the independently read anatomical distinction and source 前屈的; no diagnosis or intervention is proposed.
Drawing separate angles to distinguish uterine bending from whole-organ tilting is a meaningful teaching use of the noun; Chinese correctly keeps 前屈 separate from 前倾.
The actual arrows indicate forward-direction blood flow rather than reversal, matching the source directional adjective and Chinese 顺行 without giving clinical instructions.
The indicated model surface is front-and-side rather than back, a concrete directional adjective use; the Chinese preserves both components and the contrast.
A particular diagram locates a corner above and in front of a shaded area, using both anatomical direction components accurately rather than merely mentioning the word.
The label points at the animal's front/ventral region on its underside, matching 前腹侧的 in a concrete anatomical illustration without species-specific claims.
A uterine orientation diagram shows whole-organ forward tilt rather than simply body-to-cervix bending; the original NCBI passage independently supports the distinction and Chinese uses 前倾.
The teacher's movable model demonstrates forward tilt of the uterus, a natural concrete adjective use consistent with the source and independently checked anatomy, not a treatment claim.
